name: Mercury
description: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun, Mercury is a cratered world of extreme temperatures.
overview: Mercury completes an orbit in only 88 Earth days. Its battered surface records billions of years of impacts, while its unusually large metallic core occupies most of the planet.
facts: Mercury has no moons or rings.
A solar day lasts 176 Earth days.
Water ice exists inside permanently shadowed polar craters.

name: Venus
description: Earth’s similar-sized neighbor is wrapped in a dense atmosphere and is the hottest planet.
overview: Venus has a carbon-dioxide atmosphere and sulfuric-acid clouds that produce a runaway greenhouse effect. Its surface is dominated by volcanic plains and highlands.
facts: Venus rotates opposite most planets.
Its surface pressure is about 92 times Earth’s.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.

name: Earth
description: Our ocean world is the only known planet with life and stable liquid water at its surface.
overview: Earth’s active geology, protective magnetic field, oxygen-rich atmosphere, and abundant water support an extraordinary diversity of life.
facts: About 71% of Earth is covered by ocean.
Earth’s atmosphere is mostly nitrogen and oxygen.
Its Moon helps stabilize the planet’s axial tilt.

name: Mars
description: The Red Planet preserves evidence of ancient rivers, lakes, and a wetter planetary past.
overview: Mars is a cold desert world with giant volcanoes, deep canyons, polar ice caps, and a thin carbon-dioxide atmosphere. Robotic explorers continue to investigate its history.
facts: Olympus Mons is the largest volcano in the Solar System.
Mars has two small moons: Phobos and Deimos.
Its red color comes from iron minerals oxidizing in the soil.

name: Jupiter
description: The largest planet is a gas giant filled with powerful storms and a vast family of moons.
overview: Jupiter contains more than twice the mass of all other planets combined. Its colorful bands are shaped by fast winds, while the Great Red Spot is a centuries-old storm.
facts: Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet.
Ganymede is the Solar System’s largest moon.
Its magnetic field is the strongest of any planet.

name: Saturn
description: Saturn is a low-density gas giant encircled by the Solar System’s most spectacular rings.
overview: Saturn’s rings consist of countless particles of ice and rock. The planet’s complex moon system includes Titan, which has a thick atmosphere and methane lakes.
facts: Saturn is less dense than water.
Its rings are broad but remarkably thin.
Titan is larger than the planet Mercury.

name: Uranus
description: This pale blue ice giant rotates on its side, likely because of an ancient collision.
overview: Methane in Uranus’s atmosphere absorbs red light and gives the planet its blue-green color. Its extreme axial tilt creates seasons lasting about 21 Earth years.
facts: Uranus has 13 known rings.
It was the first planet discovered with a telescope.
Its magnetic field is sharply tilted and off-center.

name: Neptune
description: The most distant planet is a deep blue ice giant with the fastest winds in the Solar System.
overview: Neptune is a cold, dynamic world with dark storms and supersonic winds. Its largest moon, Triton, orbits backward and is probably a captured Kuiper Belt object.
facts: Neptune was predicted mathematically before it was observed.
Its winds can exceed 2,000 kilometers per hour.
Triton has active nitrogen geysers.
